title: Unramifiedness of representable stack morphisms descends along flat covers
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ a morphism of algebraic stacks over $S$ representable by algebraic spaces, and $q:W\to\mathcal B$ a surjective flat locally finitely presented morphism from an algebraic space. Put $V=W\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal A$, which is an algebraic space. Then $f$ is unramified if and only if $V\to W$ is unramified. Unramifiedness, flatness and local finite presentation use [def-weil-unramified-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] on scheme charts, and surjectivity is surjectivity after every scheme base change. An algebraic stack means a stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stack, 2-fibre product and representability by algebraic spaces use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Properties of representable morphisms are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts.

source.place: Tag 04XD (lemma-check-property-covering), for P = unramified, as listed in Section 04XB (section-properties-morphisms).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability], $q:W\to\mathcal B$ is representable by algebraic spaces, since $\mathcal B$ has representable diagonal. Fix any scheme $t:T\to\mathcal B$, and put $X_T=T\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal A$ and $W_T=T\times_{\mathcal B}W$. These are algebraic spaces, respectively by representability of $f$ and of $q$. A scheme map $E\to W_T$ gives $e:E\to T$, $w:E\to W$, and an isomorphism $\eta:t e\xrightarrow{\sim}q w$. There is a canonical equivalence over $E$, $X_T\times_T E\simeq V\times_W E$. Explicitly, on each test scheme $R$, its left-hand objects are $(z,a,\alpha)$ with $z\in E(R)$, $a\in\mathcal A(R)$ and $\alpha:t e(z)\xrightarrow{\sim}f(a)$. Send this to $(z,a,\alpha\eta_z^{-1})$ on the right, whose comparison runs from $q w(z)$ to $f(a)$. The inverse sends $(z,a,\beta)$ to $(z,a,\beta\eta_z)$. For an arrow $d:a\to a'$ over fixed $z$, its comparison equation $f(d)\alpha=\alpha'$ becomes $f(d)(\alpha\eta_z^{-1})=\alpha'\eta_z^{-1}$, exactly the right-hand arrow equation in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; the inverse check multiplies by $\eta_z$. Pullback restricts $z,\alpha,\eta$ together, so both formulas commute with base pullback and cancel. Both keep $z$, hence preserve the projection to $E$.

source.place: Tag 04XD (lemma-check-property-covering), the two cartesian squares; Tag 045G supplies representability of q.

proof.text: First assume $f$ is unramified. To test $V\to W$ on etale scheme charts, take any etale scheme chart $E\to W$ and any etale scheme chart $U\to V\times_W E$. The latter fibre product is $E\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal A$, by the same object-and-isomorphism description of the 2-fibre product. The hypothesis on $f$, applied to the scheme $E\to\mathcal B$, says precisely that $U\to E$ is unramified. These are all the source and target chart tests in the statement, so $V\to W$ is unramified. This is a definitional specialization, with no descent theorem used in this direction. Charts exist by [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 04XD, forward implication; the chartwise test is the convention of Section 04XB.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $V\to W$ is unramified and fix an arbitrary scheme $T\to\mathcal B$. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $E\to W_T$, provided by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Since $q$ is representable by step 1, [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] applies to it: $W_T\to T$, its base change, is flat and locally of finite presentation. That statement also says etale implies smooth implies flat and locally of finite presentation, so the atlas has both properties. Composition therefore makes $p:E\to T$ flat and locally of finite presentation. For surjectivity use precisely the current statement's chart criterion: for a representable surjective map $q$ and every scheme $T\to\mathcal B$, every surjective etale scheme chart $E\to W\times_{\mathcal B}T$ has surjective composite $E\to T$. Our chosen atlas is such a chart, so $p$ is surjective. Thus $p$ is a surjective flat locally finitely presented scheme morphism; no quasi-compactness of $p$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 04XD, reverse implication, the fppf cover of T; Section 04XB for base change and composition of representable properties.

proof.text: The singleton $\{p:E\to T\}$ is an fpqc covering in [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Here is the finite-affine condition explicitly. For an affine open $T_0\subset T$, cover $p^{-1}(T_0)$ by affine opens $E_j\subset E$. Their images cover $T_0$ because $p$ is surjective, and each image is open because $p$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. An affine scheme is quasi-compact by clause (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact], so finitely many $p(E_j)$ cover $T_0$. Each selected $E_j$ is an affine open of $E$ contained in $p^{-1}(T_0)$, so its image is contained in $T_0$; thus the finite union of these images equals $T_0$, as the definition requires. Together with the already established flatness of $p$, this verifies both conditions. The empty $T_0$ uses the empty finite family.

source.place: Tag 022C (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc), finite-affine argument, using openness and quasi-compactness of affine schemes.

proof.text: Let $U\to X_T$ be any representable etale scheme chart. Form the scheme $U_E=U\times_T E$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and the algebraic space $V_E=V\times_W E$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Step 1 identifies $V_E$ with $X_T\times_T E$. Under that identification $U_E\to V_E$ is the base change of $U\to X_T$, hence etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. On test points $(u,z)$ with the same image in $T$, it sends $u\mapsto(t,a,\alpha)$ to $(z,a,\alpha\eta_z^{-1})$; its composite to $E$ is $z$. Thus this composite is precisely the second projection $U\times_T E\to E$ required for descent. By [lem-sfb-space-unramified-permanence], $V_E\to E$ is unramified (base change of the hypothesized $V\to W$), $U_E\to V_E$ is unramified (it is etale), and their composite $U_E\to E$ is unramified. All the morphisms in these applications are morphisms of algebraic spaces; since $U_E$ and $E$ are schemes, the last assertion is exactly scheme unramifiedness in the chart convention.

source.place: Tag 042A (lemma-descending-property-unramified), scheme-chart reduction; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03ZJ and 03ZK for base change and chart tests.

proof.text: Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-unramified] to the scheme morphism $U\to T$ and the fpqc covering $\{E\to T\}$ established in step 4. Its required base change is exactly $U_E\to E$, proved unramified in step 5. Thus $U\to T$ is unramified. As $U\to X_T$ was an arbitrary etale scheme chart, this says that $X_T\to T$ is unramified in the convention of the statement. As $T\to\mathcal B$ was an arbitrary scheme test, $f$ is unramified. This completes the converse without assuming an atlas of $\mathcal B$ is etale or adding any finite-type, separation or quasi-compactness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 02VM (lemma-descending-property-unramified), applied to U => T; this expands the final fppf-locality invocation in stacks-properties.tex Tag 04XD.
